personal.bio:
I am currently pursuing my Master of Pharmacy (M. Pharm) in Pharmaceutics at the University Department of Chemical Technology, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University, Aurangabad.

I completed my Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) with a CGPA of 8.28 from Dadasaheb Balpande College of Pharmacy, Nagpur. My academic journey has helped me build a strong foundation in pharmaceutical sciences and develop a passion for bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application in the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors.

Driven by curiosity and a commitment to continuous learning, I aim to contribute meaningfully to research, formulation development, and clinical practice, creating real-world impact in patient care and drug innovation. 

Let’s connect—I look forward to collaborating with professionals in pharma and healthcare to create impactful solutions.

research.title: Conservation of Traditional Indian Medicine and Importance of Preservation
research.institution: Dadasaheb Balpande College of Pharmacy, Besa, Nagpur
research.abstract: Amidst the evolving landscape of healthcare, traditional Indian medicines stand as repositories of ancient wisdom, offering holistic approaches to well-being. This research delves into the critical need for conserving these invaluable medicinal traditions and the profound significance of their preservation.
highlights: Exploration of diverse traditional Indian medicine systems including Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani
Analysis of biodiversity loss and climate change impacts on medicinal plants
Methodology including literature review, biodiversity assessment, and ecological impact analysis
Emphasis on educational programs and community engagement for preservation

research.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Nutritive Capsule for Hair Damage Repairing
research.institution: Dadasaheb Balpande College of Pharmacy, Nagpur
research.abstract:
As part of my Bachelor of Pharmacy final year project, I worked on the formulation and evaluation of herbal-based nutritive capsules aimed at repairing hair damage.

 🔎👩🏻‍🔬Objective:
To develop and evaluate capsules using extracts of Hibiscus sabdariffa (Roselle) and Murraya koenigii (Curry leaves) for their nutritive and antioxidant properties.

🧪 💊Methodology:

1.Extracts were obtained and subjected to phytochemical screening.

2.Niosomes were formulated using reverse phase evaporation technique.

3.Capsules were filled and evaluated for weight variation, disintegration, stability, and permeability.

📊📑 Key Results:

Optimized niosomes (Batch-9) showed particle size ~264 nm and good stability.

Capsules passed all evaluation tests including disintegration (within 16 mins).

Herbal extracts showed high flavonoid content and antioxidant activity, supporting their role in hair nourishment and repair.

✅ Conclusion:
The study demonstrated that herbal-based nutritive capsules offer a safe and effective alternative to synthetic products for hair damage repair. Further in-vivo studies can validate their long-term efficacy

research.title: Role of Polyphenolic Agents in Cancer Prevention and Therapy via Epigenetic Pathways
research.institution: Dadasaheb Balpande College of Pharmacy, Nagpur
research.abstract:
Overview:
• Examined how polyphenols, obtained primarily from dietary sources, influence genetic and epigenetic alterations associated with tumorigenesis.

• Studied their impact on key regulatory mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNAs.

• Observed that polyphenols such as curcumin can downregulate oncogenes (e.g., HDACs) while upregulating tumor suppressor genes (e.g., HAT).

• Highlighted their role in exerting anti-carcinogenic, anti-metastatic, anti-inflammatory, and pro-apoptotic effects.

Conclusion:
The findings support the potential of polyphenolic agents as effective chemopreventive and therapeutic molecules in oncology. While results are promising, further comprehensive studies and clinical validation are essential to establish their efficacy and safety in human applications.
